title: Ananias (Acts 9:10–19)
hook: a frightened believer is sent to heal his enemy and calls him "brother Saul"

segments.voice: Yesterday, conversion: Saul in the dust on the road to Damascus, led into the city blind. Your line was the road can turn. Where did you leave an inch of room? Day eighty-one.

Imagine being told to go and knock on the door of the one person in town you're most afraid of. Not to argue. To help. That's the job handed to a man named Ananias. He's an ordinary follower of Jesus in Damascus, not an apostle, and we know almost nothing else about him. In a vision the Lord calls his name, and he answers, here I am. Then come the instructions, specific as a delivery address: go to the street called Straight, to the house of Judas, and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul. He's praying. And he's seen a vision of a man named Ananias coming to lay hands on him so he can see again. Ananias knows exactly who Saul is.
screen: `KNOCK ON THAT DOOR.` → `THE STREET CALLED STRAIGHT.` → `ASK FOR SAUL.`

segments.voice: So Ananias does what most of us would do. He objects. In the King James Bible: "Lord, I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints at Jerusalem." And he came here with papers to arrest us. I like that he says it. The Bible keeps a lot of honest objections. And the answer comes back: go, "for he is a chosen vessel unto me." Not, he's harmless. Just, go. So he goes. Walks the street called Straight, finds the house, and walks into the room where the most feared man in the movement is sitting blind. Lays his hands on him. And the first words out of his mouth are these: "Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me." Brother. Before Saul has done a single thing to earn it. Before anyone knows if he's for real. The man who came to take Ananias away in chains is greeted as family. And then, Luke says, something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see. That's where our English saying comes from: the scales fell from my eyes. He gets up, he's baptized, and he eats, for the first time in three days. Here's what's easy to miss. The famous one in this story is Saul, who'll become Paul and write a good part of the New Testament. But Paul's sight comes back through the hands of someone almost nobody remembers, who was scared, said so, and went anyway. The whole rest of Acts turns on two words from a frightened man. Brother Saul.
screen: `LORD, I HAVE HEARD OF THIS MAN.` · `A CHOSEN VESSEL. GO.` · `SCALES FALL FROM HIS EYES.` · `A NOBODY, SCARED, WHO WENT.` · then, large: `BROTHER SAUL.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: call someone brother or sister. Sit, and breathe. Bring to mind someone you keep at a distance. Not someone dangerous; someone you've quietly filed as not one of us. A neighbor, a relative, a coworker on the other side of some argument. Say their name in your head, and put brother or sister in front of it. Notice what happens in you. Resistance, maybe. Or a softening. Just notice. If you pray, you can pray for them by that name. The bell holds the time.
Ananias. The frightened disciple in Damascus who went anyway, laid his hands on his enemy, and called him brother.
Your line: brother saul. Today, give one person you've kept at a distance a word of family: a warm greeting, their name said kindly. Tomorrow, a rooftop vision and a Roman's door. Day eighty-one.

howItsDone: Christians in many churches call one another brother and sister, a habit that goes back to the first believers. Ananias of Damascus is honored as a saint in Catholic and Orthodox churches.

fork.setup: you're Ananias. you've just laid your hands on the man who came to arrest you. what is your first word to him?
fork.reveal: brother saul, the Lord, even Jesus, hath sent me. family first, before Saul has earned anything.

original.note: Greek: brother, literally from the same womb. The first Christians used it for one another.

trapdoor: what you thought: a minor character in Paul's story.
what it means: a frightened disciple objects, goes anyway, and calls his enemy brother, and Saul's sight comes back through his hands.
what a scholar hears: adelphos, from the same womb, the family word the early church used for everyone; Paul later retells this moment in Acts 22.
